sections.h2: Who handles what on a McDonald County tax bill
sections.html:
Two courthouse offices share the work. The Assessor determines values and hears questions and appeals. The Collector sends out statements, takes payments and conducts the delinquent tax sale.

  • Collector: 408 Harmon Street, Pineville, MO 64856. Mail goes to PO Box 725. Phone (417) 223-7408.
  • Assessor: McDonald County Courthouse, 408 Harmon Street, Pineville. Mail goes to PO Box 726. Phone (417) 223-4361 for real estate and mapping.
  • Both offices open weekdays 8:00 am to 4:00 pm without a lunch closure, and they close on state holidays.

The Assessor, not the Collector, changes the mailing address on a bill. If you are about to sell and the statement still goes to an old address, correct it before you list.

McDonald County fills Missouri's southwest corner, bordering Arkansas and Oklahoma, with Pineville as the county seat. Estimated population in July 2025 was 23,992, a 3.0 percent rise over the 2020 base. Of 9,940 housing units, about two in three households (67.3 percent) own their home. Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $154,700, median gross rent is $767 and household income is $52,375. Most of the county sits in the McDonald County R-I School District, with small areas in other districts, so check the district line on the tax bill when comparing homes.

Each taxable parcel is valued as of the January 1 assessment date set by state statute. The Missouri State Tax Commission supervises county assessors. Assessed value is a percentage of market value, and the percentage depends on how the property is classed.

McDonald County assessment rates by property class
Property classAssessment rate
Residential19%
Agricultural12%
Commercial32%

The tax rate then comes from every taxing body covering the parcel, such as school districts, road districts, cities, fire districts and a junior college. The Assessor's site adds that the county government itself gets no property tax levy for operations and depends on sales tax.

RSMo 137.115 has assessors set new values on January 1 of odd-numbered years and carry them through the next even year, with new construction as the exception. It also bars raising a residential parcel by more than 15 percent without a physical inspection, again excluding new construction.

Statements for personal property and real estate go out in the first week of November. A bill is payable on arrival and becomes delinquent after December 31. This year's mailing is already out, so the due date is December 31, 2026.

  • You may pay every statement with one check, but the Collector cannot take a partial payment.
  • Cash, personal check, money order and credit card are all accepted, at the counter, by mail or online.
  • A payment postmarked after December 31 comes back unprocessed unless it includes the late fees.
  • No statement by the end of November? Call the Collector. A bill that never arrived does not erase the debt, penalty or interest.

Missouri adds a penalty to unpaid taxes after the delinquency date (RSMo 139.100). Phone the Collector at (417) 223-7408 for the current penalty and interest percentages before paying late. A mailed payment counts as paid on its postmark date.

The delinquent tax sale takes place every August. An owner with old unpaid bills can find a parcel heading to auction well before noticing.

sections.h2: How do I contest my McDonald County value?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor at (417) 223-4361 and ask for an informal hearing. Bring sales of comparable homes nearby, repair estimates or photos that back up a lower figure. Ask the same office when the local equalization board takes filings.

If the board leaves your value alone, RSMo 138.430 allows an appeal to the State Tax Commission, due by the statutory deadline or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later. While an appeal is pending, the disputed taxes sit in a separate impound fund rather than going to the taxing bodies.

Paying under protest is another route. Under RSMo 139.031, you pay the entire bill before it turns delinquent and give the collector a written statement of your grounds. If no circuit court suit against the collector follows within ninety days, the protest is void. A pending State Tax Commission appeal takes the place of that suit.

The Missouri Department of Revenue runs the Property Tax Credit Claim, widely called the circuit breaker. Certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals can claim a credit for part of the property tax or rent they paid, up to $1,100 for owners who live in their own home and $750 for renters. The amount turns on taxes paid and total household income, taxable and nontaxable. Send questions to PropertyTaxCredit@dor.mo.gov.

A homestead exemption also exists for a former prisoner of war with a total service-connected disability. The owner must live in the home as a primary residence and show the assessor a Department of Veterans Affairs letter plus discharge papers or a records center letter confirming prisoner of war status.

Service members stationed in the county on orders, with a home of record outside Missouri, generally owe no Missouri personal property tax on non-business items.

Count the tax bill as part of the closing. Before listing, call the Collector and ask about every year on the parcel, then let the closing agent split the current year between buyer and seller. A parcel with delinquent years can land in the August sale, so settle older balances first.

  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address on file with the Assessor.
  • Ask the Collector for a payoff figure on each parcel you sell, including land and any manufactured home.
  • Save your settlement statement, which records how the year's tax was divided.
  • If the assessed value looks high, take it up with the Assessor ahead of the board deadline, not after closing.

Back taxes can slow a conventional sale because the title company will not close over an open balance. A buyer paying cash can often close faster, since there is no lender waiting on a clean tax record, though the unpaid amount still has to be cleared from your proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: What date makes a McDonald County tax bill late?
faqs.a: Anything unpaid after December 31. Bills go out the first week of November, and a payment postmarked in January comes back unless late fees are included.

faqs.q: Can I pay half of my bill now and half later?
faqs.a: No. The Collector cannot accept partial payment, though all statements can be paid together with a single check.

faqs.q: What assessment rate applies to a McDonald County house?
faqs.a: Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value. Farmland is 12 percent and commercial parcels are 32 percent, before any taxing body applies its levy.

faqs.q: Where do I send an address correction for my tax statement?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's office at (417) 223-4361. The Collector's site sends address changes there.

faqs.q: When is the delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: The Collector holds it each August. Call (417) 223-7408 for the exact date and the parcels listed.
